stem: Which statements correctly distinguish common federal OUD medication pathways? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Buprenorphine-naloxone remains Schedule III; the naloxone component does not make the product noncontrolled
Methadone for ongoing OUD maintenance is not handled as an ordinary community-pharmacy Schedule II pain prescription outside the applicable narcotic-treatment framework
Methadone and buprenorphine are legally interchangeable simply because both can treat OUD
Buprenorphine becomes Schedule VI in Massachusetts when used for OUD
A qualifying buprenorphine Schedule III prescription for OUD can use the ordinary prescription-dispensing framework when all current prescribing requirements are met

explanation.core_reasoning: Buprenorphine products and methadone can both treat OUD but follow materially different controlled-substance treatment pathways.

choice_analysis.C: Their schedules and treatment pathways differ.
choice_analysis.D: Indication does not remove federal Schedule III status.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule III-V narcotic treatment can have a prescription pathway.

related_facts: Massachusetts quantity limits are a separate issue from federal treatment authority.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating all MOUD products as one legal class.

reasoning_steps: Distinguish Schedule III prescription pathway from Schedule II methadone maintenance
Apply product status without indication-based reclassification
